claims.text: The initial material is a random equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr solid solution.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has significant local lattice distortion.
Random HfNbTaTiZr has a broadened high-frequency phonon DOS.
Thermal annealing or Monte Carlo evolution can induce chemical short-range order in HfNbTaTiZr.
The induced short-range order nucleates B2-like HfTi and TiZr binary clusters.
The B2-like HfTi and TiZr clusters can percolate while the alloy remains an overall single-phase BCC structure.
A temperature range of 800–1200 K is sufficient for SRO evolution in HfNbTaTiZr while remaining below the solvus for phase separation.
Ordering reduces the variance of bond lengths and bond angles inside the B2-like domains.
Reduced bond-length and bond-angle variance lowers the phonon scattering cross-section and narrows high-frequency phonon linewidths.
The random-to-ordered transition reduces fluctuations in the local potential-energy landscape and therefore reduces chemical-disorder scattering.
B2-like ordering reduces the RMS atomic displacement amplitude.
Reduced RMS displacement enhances the group velocity and lifetime of high-frequency optical and acoustic phonons.
Percolating ordered clusters provide continuous low-scattering pathways through which phonons can traverse the material.
The reduction in disorder scattering outweighs scattering from the remaining disordered regions and increases lattice thermal conductivity relative to the random state.
The conductivity increase is accompanied by sharper high-frequency phonon-DOS peaks.
The conductivity increase is accompanied by lower Debye-Waller factors for Hf, Ti, and Zr atoms in the ordered clusters.
Random equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has ultralow thermal conductivity because of mass variance and lattice distortion.
A conductivity increase occurs only once ordered clusters exceed a percolation threshold; below that threshold the alloy remains in the lower-conductivity disordered regime.
Growth of ordered regions into distinct precipitates or development of a large chemical or interfacial mismatch can reverse the conductivity increase by making interface scattering dominant.
Annealing temperature and composition can control whether an ordered B2 state remains homogeneous or decomposes into ordered B2 and disordered BCC regions.
